nodes.summary: In the space $C((0, 1))$ of continuous real functions on the open interval $(0, 1)$, with the compact-open topology (uniform convergence on compact subsets), the set of functions that have a derivative at every point of $(0, 1)$ is not a Borel set.
nodes.title: Everywhere differentiable functions do not form a Borel set

nodes.summary: A continuous function $f \colon (0, 1) \to \mathbb{R}$ has a derivative at every point if for every $x \in (0, 1)$ the function $\tilde f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ equal to $f$ on $(0, 1)$ and to $0$ outside $(0, 1)$ is differentiable at $x$. Since $\tilde f$ agrees with $f$ near every point of $(0, 1)$, this depends only on $f$: it says that $f$ is differentiable at every point of $(0, 1)$.
nodes.title: Functions differentiable at every point of $(0, 1)$
